query.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT region FROM flechtwerk.wildfire_sweeps ORDER BY region

panels.title: Active fires — marker size = detections, colour = peak FRP (MW)
panels.description: Big markers are the clustered fire objects the tracker holds in state, sized by how many 375 m hotspot pixels they have absorbed and coloured by their hottest pixel. The small translucent dots underneath are the raw detections of the last 24 h — the evidence the clusters are built from. A detection is a pixel that contained fire, not a point source. Both layers are GROUPED (by fire_id and detection_id) so a fire or pixel inside two overlapping watch regions draws once, not twice; the `regions` field lists every region that sees it. The view opens world-scale because a watch region can be anywhere; zoom to yours (Grafana's auto-fit view is not honoured by the ClickHouse datasource here).

targets.rawSql: SELECT fire_id, arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArray(region), ', ') AS regions, max(detections) AS detections, round(max(frp_max), 1) AS frp, max(last_seen) AS seen_at, avg(lat) AS latitude, avg(lon) AS longitude FROM flechtwerk.wildfire_active FINAL WHERE status = 'active' AND region IN ($region) AND as_of > now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR GROUP BY fire_id
SELECT any(lat) AS latitude, any(lon) AS longitude FROM flechtwerk.wildfire_detections WHERE region IN ($region) AND acquired_at > now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR GROUP BY detection_id

panels.title: Active fires now
panels.description: Distinct fires burning now, read from the ReplacingMergeTree FINAL. Counted with uniqExact(fire_id), not count(): the tracker holds one fire object per watch region, so a fire inside two overlapping regions occupies two state buckets and would otherwise be counted twice. Because a fire_id is derived from its founding detection, both regions name it identically — which is what makes this dedupe possible. A fire leaves the count when a sweep marker finds it unseen for 12 h of event time.

targets.rawSql: SELECT uniqExact(fire_id) AS active_fires FROM flechtwerk.wildfire_active FINAL WHERE status = 'active' AND region IN ($region) AND as_of > now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR

panels.title: Largest active fires
panels.description: Ranked by absorbed detections, one row per distinct fire (grouped by fire_id, so a fire seen by two overlapping watch regions appears once — `regions` lists which). `burning_for` is last_seen − first_seen in event time, so it measures the observed lifetime of the cluster, not wall-clock age.

targets.rawSql: SELECT * FROM (SELECT fire_id, arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArray(region), ', ') AS regions, max(detections) AS detections, round(max(frp_max), 1) AS frp_max, round(max(frp_sum), 1) AS frp_sum, min(first_seen) AS started, dateDiff('second', min(first_seen), max(last_seen)) AS burning_for FROM flechtwerk.wildfire_active FINAL WHERE status = 'active' AND region IN ($region) AND as_of > now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR GROUP BY fire_id) ORDER BY detections DESC, frp_max DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Total fire radiative power per region (MW, sweep-paced)
panels.description: Summed frp_sum across every active fire, one point per sweep. Because status is emitted per sweep rather than per detection, this line has a steady cadence even while nothing new is being detected — which is exactly what the sweep marker is for.

targets.rawSql: SELECT as_of AS time, region, sum(frp_sum) AS frp FROM flechtwerk.wildfire_status WHERE status = 'active' AND region IN ($region) AND $__timeFilter(as_of) GROUP BY time, region ORDER BY time

panels.title: Fire log — ignition / merged / extinguished
panels.description: The sparse lifecycle stream, newest first, kept without a TTL. `merged_into` is set only on a merge (two hotspot groups turned out to be one blaze). An extinguished fire followed by an ignition in the same place is the documented self-healing case: a false extinction repairing itself.

targets.rawSql: SELECT occurred_at AS time, kind, region, fire_id, detections, round(frp_max, 1) AS frp_max, merged_into FROM flechtwerk.wildfire_events WHERE region IN ($region) AND $__timeFilter(occurred_at) ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 200

panels.title: Poll heartbeat — is the watch alive? (sweep markers)
panels.description: Read from the sweep markers, not the detections: a region with nothing burning still sweeps, so a fresh age here means "polling fine, no fires" while a stale age means the ingest stage has stopped. That distinction is the whole reason the marker is emitted even on a quiet poll — and it matters because no input means no time means no extinction.

targets.rawSql: SELECT region, max(sweep_at) AS last_sweep, dateDiff('second', max(sweep_at), now()) AS age_seconds, count() AS sweeps, sum(new_detections) AS new_detections FROM flechtwerk.wildfire_sweeps WHERE region IN ($region) AND $__timeFilter(sweep_at) GROUP BY region ORDER BY region
